issue_context.title: Plugwise Smile Anna shows OnOff Heating incorrectly sometimes
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I found a problem with my Plugwise Smile Anna heating `binary_sensor.onoff_heating`. It is showing sometimes the inverse of the actual state of the heating system.
I have an OnOff, not an OpenTherm system, so that can be the cause. 

I looked at the `core/domain_objects` xml output and saw that the value of `intended_central_heating_state` was showing `on`, but the value of `central_heating_state` was `off` and that was the correct value.
This invalid state was shown the whole day and eventually corrected itself the next morning.

It seems that the value of `intended_central_heating_state` is not the correct value for an OnOff system and the `central_heating_state` should be used.


![Screenshot_20221109-085124_DuckDuckGo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21026753/200784027-f6a7bfac-c4f3-48c2-93b4-891722485672.jpg)

review_comments:
The PR description says:

> When not a number, show as sensor (when available)

However, this always creates the sensor it is not a replacement/instead of the number, right?

This only creates the sensor when it's in the data as a sensor and not as a number:
Sensor: `"sensors": {"sensor_name_1": value, "sensor_name_2": value, ...}`
Number: `"number_name": {"setpoint": value, ...}`

I've made sure that the library never output's both (the library first picks up the sensor, when it's available as a number the sensor-data is overwritten).

And no sensor is created when it's not in the output provided by the library.
